title: French Onion Soup
subtitle: Classic Parisian onion soup with Gruyère croûtons
excerpt: The definitive French onion soup: deeply caramelised onions in a rich beef broth, poured into bowls, topped with toasted bread, and blanketed in melted Gruyère until bubbling and golden. Patience with the onions is everything.

recipe.sourceNotes: French onion soup (soupe à l'oignon gratinée) is one of the most iconic dishes of Parisian bistro cooking, traditionally associated with the workers' markets of Les Halles and served in the early hours of the morning. The foundation is the long, patient caramelisation of a large quantity of onions until they are deeply golden and sweet; this process cannot be rushed, typically taking 45 to 60 minutes over gentle heat. The caramelised onions are then simmered in beef stock and often enriched with white wine or cognac. The final finishing step, the gratin, involves topping the soup with rounds of toasted bread and a generous layer of Gruyère and grilling until bubbling and golden. The quality of the beef stock is critical to the depth of the finished soup.

content.text: The onions must caramelise slowly and deeply; this takes 45 to 60 minutes and cannot be shortened. Rushing the process produces bitter, unevenly cooked onions and a pale soup that lacks the characteristic sweetness and depth. Use ovenproof soup bowls that can go under the grill directly from the oven.

Melt the butter with the oil in a large, heavy-based pot. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes, for 45 to 60 minutes until the onions are deeply golden, very soft, and reduced to about a quarter of their original volume.
Add the garlic and flour. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the wine and brandy if using. Increase the heat and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the stock, bay leaves, and thyme. Simmer for 20 minutes. Season.

Preheat the grill to its highest setting. Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls placed on a baking tray. Float 2 toasted baguette slices on each. Pile the Gruyère generously on top. Grill for 3 to 5 minutes until the cheese is bubbling, golden, and slightly charred at the edges. Serve immediately.
